question: We're developing a sunless-look tinted moisturizer and want to use β-carotene as the colorant. May we, and what restrictions, certification or labeling apply?
key_elements: Yes. 73.2095(b) lists β-carotene for coloring cosmetics generally, including cosmetics intended for use in the area of the eye, in amounts consistent with good manufacturing practice (no numeric cap). It must conform in identity and specifications to § 73.95(a)(1) and (b) ((a)). The additive and its color mixtures bear § 70.25 labeling ((c)). Batches are exempt from section 721(c) certification ((d)).

73.2095.head: (a) Identity and specifications. The color additive β-carotene shall conform in identity and specifications to the requirements of § 73.95(a)(1) and (b).
73.2095.tail: -carotene shall conform in identity and specifications to the requirements of § 73.95(a)(1) and (b).

73.2095.head: (b) Uses and restrictions. The color additive β-carotene may be safely used in coloring cosmetics generally, including cosmetics intended for use in the area of
73.2095.tail: cs intended for use in the area of the eye, in amounts consistent with good manufacturing practices.

73.2095.head: (c) Labeling. The color additive and any mixture prepared therefrom intended solely or in part for coloring purposes shall bear, in addition to any information
73.2095.tail: information required by law, labeling in accordance with the provisions of § 70.25 of this chapter.
